audit.whatIsWrong: Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds is absent from both layers, while the entry repeatedly leans on Soul Eater lifesteal as the reason Nasus survives — whys[1] 'your Soul Eater lifesteal heals it off', wants.you[2] 'lifesteal to grind his drain-tank HP'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Singed drinks a potent brew of chemicals, granting him increased combat stats, and making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds.' The kit's derived flag is antiHeal. From level 6 onward, the moment Singed ults, the lifesteal this entire entry is built on gets cut for as long as he keeps poison on you. That inverts the extended-fight maths and it appears nowhere. This is also a case _missing-interactions.json could not catch, because that file flags enemies who heal, not enemies who apply anti-heal to you.
audit.corrected: Insanity Potion (100s cooldown) makes his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds — while it is up, Soul Eater lifesteal stops carrying the fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive is never named in the content layer, and the Fling combo is described as being flung into the poison — mid 'he lays poison trail, Flings you into it', wants.foe[1] 'Drop poison trail and Fling you onto it'.
audit.why: Fling: 'Damages target enemy unit and flings them into the air behind Singed. If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' The dangerous sequence is W then E, not Q then E — landing in the adhesive is what converts a displacement into a root, and the root is the only hard lock Singed has on Nasus in the entire matchup. Being flung into poison is just damage you walk out of. The full layer's dontsFull[1] is titled 'Get E-flipped into goo', so that layer knows about the combo the content layer describes wrongly.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive first, Fling second — landing in the adhesive roots you. Poison alone does not.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'late' refers to 'his ult's HP-swap fight'.
audit.why: Insanity Potion has no health swap of any kind — it grants combat stats and adds Grievous Wounds to Poison Trail. There is nothing in Singed's current kit that swaps health. This looks like a leftover from an older kit or a confusion with another champion, and it tells a Nasus to fear a mechanic that does not exist while the mechanic that actually matters (anti-heal) goes unmentioned in the same sentence.
audit.corrected: Replace the HP-swap claim with the real ultimate effect: stats plus Grievous Wounds on his poison.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Confirmed — no numbers in either layer.
audit.why: The decisive numbers are Fling at 10/9.5/9/8.5/8 with a range of only 125, Mega Adhesive at 17/16/15/14/13 with 1000 range, and Insanity Potion at a flat 100s. Fling's 125 range in particular is the whole reason the lane is survivable: Singed has to be practically inside you to throw it, while Wither reaches 700. Nothing in the entry gives the player that comparison.
audit.corrected: Fling 10s at rank 1 and only 125 range; Mega Adhesive 17s at rank 1; Insanity Potion 100s flat. Wither out-ranges Fling by 575.

audit.whatIsWrong: Noxious Slipstream is never mentioned, though the entry twice warns against chasing him.
audit.why: 'Singed drafts off nearby champions, gaining a burst of Move Speed when passing them.' The chase is not merely futile, it actively powers his escape — passing near you is what grants the speed. That converts a vague 'don't chase' into a mechanical reason a player will actually remember.
audit.corrected: Noxious Slipstream gives him a move-speed burst for passing nearby champions, so chasing him is what fuels the getaway.

edits.before: His biggest threat window: poison trail plus Fling chunks you and he tries to bait your tower or freeze you off CS while he out-sustains.
edits.after: His real combo is Mega Adhesive then Fling into it — landing in the adhesive roots you. Fling reaches only 125, so stay off him.

edits.after: Both become unkillable splitpushers — but Insanity Potion makes his poison apply Grievous Wounds, which cuts your lifesteal.

edits.after: Land Wither from 700 range — Fling only reaches 125, so he must come to you

edits.before: Drop poison trail and Fling you onto it, then kite away on raw move speed before Wither lands
edits.after: Drop Mega Adhesive and Fling you into it for the root, then kite off on raw move speed

edits.after: Ult into Insanity Potion so his poison applies Grievous Wounds and your lifesteal drops off

edits.before: Singed barely fights you levels 1-3 — he proxies the wave behind your tower and the lane becomes a stacking contest, which actually suits you fine. Don't chase him into the river or his jungle to contest the proxy; his raw move speed and poison trail mean you'll eat damage for nothing and never land an auto. Just take the free farm he leaves, hit your Q on every cannon, and don't let him Fling you under his own tower for a cheap dive setup.
edits.after: Singed barely fights you levels 1-3 — he proxies the wave behind your tower and the lane becomes a stacking contest, which suits you fine. Don't chase him into the river or his jungle: Noxious Slipstream hands him a move-speed burst for passing nearby champions, so the chase itself is what fuels his escape. Take the free farm he leaves, Q every cannon, and never let him Fling you under his own tower.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where Singed is most annoying: he lays poison trail, Flings you into it, and kites off on pure move speed before your single-target W can connect. The trick is to hold Wither for the exact moment he commits a Fling — slow his move speed to a crawl and he can't run the poison loop, and your Spirit Fire's armor shred plus lifesteal lets you grind him. At 6 your Fury of the Sands lets you survive his all-in, but don't over-extend chasing a Singed with Flash up; he wins the foot race every time.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where Singed is most annoying, and the combo to fear is Mega Adhesive first and Fling second — land in live adhesive and you are rooted, not merely displaced. Hold Wither for the moment he commits Fling; it reaches only 125 units, so he has to be on top of you to throw it at all. Then Spirit Fire's armor shred plus lifesteal grinds him down. At 6, don't over-extend chasing a Singed who still has Flash up; he wins the foot race every single time.

edits.before: Late game this is two splitpush monsters who can't kill each other — you out-DPS him in a Wither'd duel, but he simply runs away with move speed and Rylai/Liandry tankiness rather than dying, so a clean solo kill is rare. Win the lane on stacks and CS, not kills: a Nasus with a big stack lead and Wither out-sidelanes a Singed who can only stall. Never face-tank his ult's HP-swap fight off-cooldown, and keep Wither for when his team tries to let him run you down in skirmishes.
edits.after: Late game this is two splitpush monsters who can't kill each other — you out-DPS him in a Wither'd duel, but he runs rather than dies, so a clean solo kill is rare. Insanity Potion is the real problem: a flat 100s cooldown, and while it is up his Poison Trail applies Grievous Wounds, so Soul Eater lifesteal stops carrying the fight. Win the lane on stacks and CS rather than kills, and hold Wither for the team skirmish where he tries to run you down.

edits.after: Poison Trail chips you and Soul Eater lifesteal heals it off — true only until Insanity Potion comes online at 6.

edits.after: His power window: Mega Adhesive into Fling roots you, and he freezes you off stacks before your items land.

edits.after: Singed wins by rooting you with Fling into Mega Adhesive and out-sustaining you.

edits.after: - Fling: 10s at rank 1, and only 125 range. - Mega Adhesive: 17s at rank 1 — a Fling into it roots you.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Fling: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Wait for Mega Adhesive to be spent before you commit — Fling into live adhesive roots you, while Fling alone only displaces.

notes: The packet suspectName for 'mid' — 'Spirit Fire's' — is a FALSE POSITIVE. Spirit Fire is Nasus's own E and is spelled correctly; the detector matched an owner ability against Singed's ability list. Same class of false positive as the Ryze and Sett entries in my slice. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: Mega Adhesive carries the 'grounding' flag, described in the kit as 'shuts off enemy dashes'. Nasus has no dash, so under the relevance rule I wrote nothing about it. I am aware that Grounded in League is generally understood to block Flash as well, which WOULD matter here — but that is not stated anywhere in the kit file, it falls squarely in the needsResearch category the brief tells me not to infer from, and getting it wrong in either direction changes whether a player thinks he can Flash out of the adhesive. Worth a League Wiki check on Mega Adhesive's grounding scope; if it does block Flash, that deserves its own line in this matchup because Flash is the escape a Nasus reaches for when rooted next to a Singed.
